name: Interior Weather
description: A quiet, devastating flat-screen film about three siblings — Tomás, Ife, and Yuki Restrepo-Mwangi — who return to their childhood Tier 2 apartment after their mother's death and discover she had been secretly documenting corporate labor violations for twenty years. The film is almost entirely set within a single apartment and relies on performance rather than technology; director Claudine Abubakar-Schwarz shot it in nine days on equipment she built herself. It circulated on physical media for two years before an underground mesh release.
cultural_impact: Interior Weather is credited with reviving flat-screen filmmaking as a deliberate artistic and political choice rather than a poverty constraint, inspiring a wave of Tier 2 directors to reject neural-feed production.
story_hooks: The mother's actual documentation — used as a prop in the film — is real and was provided by a source the director has never publicly identified.
Meridian Logistics Group quietly acquired the building where the film was shot and demolished it six months after release.
One of the sibling actors disappeared into the unincorporated zones shortly after the mesh release and has been sending encrypted messages to the director.
